unit: Log Inbound / Append Next Action idempotency_key expressions
description: Two deliveries of the same Gmail message, differing only in write-time fields, must produce byte-identical idempotency keys.
why_it_exists: communication_id is generated inside Validate Reply JSON as 'COM-' + new Date().toISOString(), so it genuinely differs between two runs. If the idempotency key were built from it, or from any other write-time value, replay protection would fail and the same inbound reply would be logged twice and would spawn a second next action.
assertions: K1: the Log Inbound idempotency_key is identical across a replay.
K2: the Append Next Action idempotency_key is identical across a replay.
K3: the key matches /^[^|]+\|[^|]+$/ and contains neither the substring 'undefined' nor 'null' - an unresolved expression must not silently become part of a key.
K4: at least one mapped column (communication_id) does differ across the replay, proving the fixture is a genuine replay and not a copy of one item.
K5: the key is stable while that volatile column changes.
K6: the key derives only from matter_id and the Gmail provider message id - no clock, no counter, no row number.
The keys are evaluated by an n8n Set node, not by test code, so what is compared is the expression engine's own output for the exact strings mapped in production.

MERGED: the keys are matter_id|provider_message_id and matter_id|provider_message_id|next_action_type; neither communication_id nor received_at enters either key.
target_unresolved_reason: The two keys are n8n Set-node expressions on Log Inbound / Append Next Action, not a Code node. Nothing in harness/units/ evaluates them.
